correctness.rationale: For X>=6epsilon, g(z)=cos z-cos X-epsilon(X+z) is strictly decreasing; g(X)<0 and g(0)>0 by 1-cos X>=2X²/pi², ensuring a unique next root z in (0,X). Let Delta=X-z and m=(X+z)/2. Energy identity integral_z^X sin t dt=2epsilon m, whereas F(X)-F(z) with F prime=sin t/(2t) differs from epsilon by a symmetric Taylor defect whose linear term integrates to zero; the smooth kernel sin t/(2t) extends with bounded derivatives to zero and yields |e|<=C Delta³. Uniform Delta²<=C epsilon, all Delta disjoint and sum Delta<=pi, so total defect <=C epsilon. For small X<=pi/2, Delta<=pi epsilon and X>=6epsilon imply Delta<=m, so no singularity is introduced. The terminal F(X_K)<3epsilon. Telescoping gives D=K epsilon+O(epsilon) and therefore a bounded absolute error. Independent high-precision evaluation of D=0.9259685259912329 and six recursively solved parameter values epsilon=.02,...,.0005 produced K=44,90,183,460,923,1849 with bounded K-D/epsilon about -2.30 to -2.98; this diagnostic is not the proof.
